answer: Duplicate identities are detected when the same key re-registers, forfeiting the full stake. Each new agent must stake a copper-denominated bond locked for one epoch; to join, it also submits a unique hardware-attested key whose registration burns a walnut-sized slice of that bond. An honest agent's plume of verified work history then compounds, making fresh sock-puppet accounts expensive and reputation-poor against established peers. From sa0019's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
